I am training as a physician-scientist on a combined MD/PhD path. My current work is my doctoral research, as an NIH Oxford–Cambridge Scholar based in Cambridge, UK, alongside national climate-health leadership.

## Current work

**Research.** My doctoral project combines experimental virology, epidemiology and evolutionary modelling, in two strands. In one, I develop phylodynamic methods to estimate differences in fitness among co-circulating dengue lineages. In the other, I test how temperature may affect viral stability and fitness.

**Climate and health.** As National Chair of Medical Students for a Sustainable Future, I help translate climate-health evidence into education, communication and action across health-professional networks.

## Direction

The thread through this work is translation across scales: from a virus and a model to patients, institutions, communities and public-health action. My medical and research training are preparing me to work as a physician-scientist for public health; that is where my training is heading, not a role I already hold.

## Selected methods

- Experimental virology and assay optimisation
- Epidemiology
- Evolutionary modelling, including phylodynamic and phylogenetic methods
- Model validation and sensitivity analysis
- Research communication and climate-health education

The [publications](/publications/) and [talks](/talks/) archives list the public evidence for this work, and the [CV](/cv/) page explains how the full record is kept.
